subject: Elevated 503s from aero-lite — remediation plan and postmortem commitments
messages:
From: Alex Barnes <alex@starlabs.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-20T15:03:21-07:00
Subject: Elevated 503s from 'aero-lite' — impact and request for status

Hi Kimberly,

We started seeing an uptick in 503/timeout responses from the aero-lite model in our production environment starting ~14:52 PDT today. Error rate jumped from ~0.2% to ~6% over a 20-minute window and is still elevated. A few details:

- Example request IDs: req_8a1f, req_8a2b, req_8a7e (timestamps attached).
- Traffic pattern: standard steady traffic (no spike on our side).
- Impact: our customer-facing inference path is failing intermittently; rollback to a cached fallback is happening but increases latency substantially.

Can you confirm if you’re seeing model-level anomalies on aero-lite and advise ETA for remediation? We have a feature release scheduled tomorrow morning and would like to understand risk.

Thanks,
Alex Barnes
Head of Platform — Starlabs
alex@starlabs.ai

Attachment: sample-req-ids.txt (txt)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Barnes <alex@starlabs.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-20T15:37:10-07:00
Subject: Re: Elevated 503s from 'aero-lite' — remediation plan and postmortem commitments

Hi Alex — thanks for the heads up and the sample IDs. We’re actively investigating. Quick update and immediate mitigation steps we’ve started: 

- Identified elevated 5xx rates for the aero-lite model group in us-west region correlated with kernel allocation failures on a subset of GPU hosts.
- Temporarily enabled model fallback routing (requests will route to aero-medium for eligible requests) to reduce 503 exposure while preserving correctness. This is live now and should reduce visible failures within minutes.
- Enabled a conservative circuit-breaker and short client-side retry guidance (we recommend 1 retry with 300ms jitter).

We need a small set of additional logs from you (you included three IDs already — that’s helpful). If you can share any X-Redwood-Request-Id headers or a snippet of the failing payloads that would speed triage.

We’ll follow up with a timeline and a root-cause summary within 48 hours. I’ve looped in Rishi (runtime) and Ben (customer ops) to coordinate triage and credits respectively.

Attachment: initial-mitigation-checklist.txt (txt)

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Date: 2025-07-20T16:02:05-07:00
Subject: [Internal] Aero-lite 503 spike — triage notes and action items

Team — quick internal summary from initial ops triage (notes pulled from telemetry and ops traces):

- Timeline: scheduler v2.4 rollout began 2025-07-19 22:10 UTC; aero-lite quantized kernels saw increased KV cache churn starting 2025-07-20 14:45 PDT; first user reports 14:52 PDT.
- Symptom: transient allocation/initialization failures from the optimized quantized path causing the serving binary to return 5xx rather than gracefully falling back.
- Root cause (preliminary): regression in kernel selection heuristics in conjunction with a new async allocator path in the runtime. The allocator path can under specific memory fragmentation patterns fail allocation checks and surface as 5xx. Not a customer workload issue.

Immediate actions (we did / are doing):
- Rolled back scheduler weight change for aero-lite shards to the previous stable config (complete).
- Disabled the async allocator path on affected hosts and forced deterministic allocator for aero-lite while we validate (in progress).
- Enabled a targeted canary routing to aero-medium for 5% of traffic during validation window.
- Added throttling at the edge for high-concurrency requests to reduce pressure while we stabilize.

Longer-term fixes (next 1–2 weeks):
- Patch kernel selection heuristics and harden allocator to gracefully degrade to CPU fallback on allocation failures (engineering PR in review, JIRA INF-4821).
- Add runtime health checks to detect allocation thrash and proactively route away from affected hosts.
- Post-deployment verification and capacity tests for quantized model paths.

Customer-facing commitments:
- Provide a customer postmortem by EOD 2025-07-22 (Kim to send).
- Offer billing credit for measurable impact window (Ben, please propose %).

Ben — can you handle the credit proposal and engagement with Starlabs? Rishi — can you own the patch, PR link, and verification plan? I’ll coordinate comms.

Attachment: ops-triage.log (txt)

— Kim

Subject: Re: Elevated 503s from 'aero-lite' — remediation plan and postmortem commitments

Hi Alex — following up with the promised postmortem and next steps. TL;DR: we identified a runtime regression introduced as part of a scheduler + allocator rollout that increased memory fragmentation on specific hosts. This led to transient allocation failures for the aero-lite quantized execution path and produced elevated 5xxs. We’ve stabilized the fleet and shipped a short-term patch; below is the full summary.

What happened (timeline):
- 2025-07-19 22:10 UTC: scheduler v2.4 rollout begins (internal change to shard weights and async allocator enabled on the fleet).
- 2025-07-20 14:45 PDT: increased KV cache churn observed for aero-lite quantized executors on subset of hosts.
- 2025-07-20 14:52 PDT: customer-facing 5xx spike; Starlabs report received at 15:03 PDT.
- 2025-07-20 15:30–16:30 PDT: enabled fallback routing to aero-medium and conservative circuit breakers; reduced user-visible failures.
- 2025-07-20 16:00 PDT: rolled back scheduler weight change for affected shards.
- 2025-07-21 03:00 UTC: disabled async allocator on impacted hosts and deployed a deterministic allocator for aero-lite.
- 2025-07-21–22: validation and canarying continued; full fleet stabilization confirmed by 2025-07-21 18:00 PDT.

Root cause (short):
- Regression in kernel selection + async allocator interaction that under high KV cache churn in the quantized path produced allocation failures rather than graceful fallback, causing 5xx responses.

Customer impact and scope:
- Affected model: aero-lite in us-west only.
- Incident window with elevated 5xxs: ~14:45–18:00 PDT on 2025-07-20 (visible spike, reduced after mitigations).
- Starlabs: intermittent user-facing failures; we observed your request IDs in our traces and matched the error patterns.

What we did to remediate:
- Immediate: fallback routing to aero-medium for eligible requests; enabled circuit breakers and client retry guidance.
- Short-term: rolled back the scheduler weight change and disabled async allocator on affected hosts.
- Patch: deployed a defensive fix that forces graceful fallback on allocation failures; PR merged and canary validated (JIRA INF-4821).
- Ongoing: runtime health checks and capacity tests; enhanced telemetry for earlier detection.

Customer commitments:
- Postmortem deliverable (this message + attached PDF).
- Billing: we will apply a 12% credit to your July invoice to account for measurable impact. Ben will follow up with formal credit note.
- Technical follow-up: Rishi will schedule a short sync next week to walk through the patch and verification steps if you’d like.

Preventive actions we’re taking:
- Improved pre-release canarying for scheduler/runtime combos.
- Additional unit/integration tests around allocator fallback paths.
- Expanded observability on quantized kernel allocations and KV cache churn.

Attached: postmortem-aero-lite-20250722.pdf (pdf)
Related: https://drive.redwood.com/file/d/1a2b3c-aero-lite-postmortem, JIRA INF-4821

We’re sorry for the disruption and appreciate the rapid report from your team which helped shorten the impact window. Let me know if you want a technical walkthrough next week; we can also schedule a post-incident retro with your SREs.
